summary: Current 1948 L-4 groundhouse on Sex Peak, staffed until the mid-1970s, NHLR-listed in 1996, refurbished into a Forest Service rental cabin in 1986.

access.note: Accessible by car via forest roads; easterly loop road segment subject to seasonal closures.

events.note: First lookout; Recreation.gov says 'early 1920s' while firelookout.com describes the first cab as '1930 vintage' — sources disagree on the date.
Current L-4 groundhouse with catwalk built, replacing the earlier cab.
Refurbished and placed in the Forest Service cabin rental program.
Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 179 on August 20, 1996.

evidence.supports: named by two foresters in 1920s, L-4 built 1948, staffed to mid-1970s, rental since 1986
evidence.quote: Sex Peak Lookout was named by two Forest Service foresters in the 1920s, reportedly after the topic of conversation that day. ... The L-4 groundhouse with catwalk was constructed in 1948 and staffed until the mid-1970s. It was refurbished and placed in the rental program in 1986.

evidence.supports: named by Anderson and Baker, naming story, plane incident, first cab 1930-vintage, replaced 1948, staffed to mid-1970s, rental 1986, 1967 staffer Hubenthal
evidence.quote: The peak was named by forester I.V. Anderson and Harry Baker, supervisor of the Cabinet National Forest in the 1920's. ... It lived up to its name when a patrol plane buzzed the lookout at eye level in the 1960's and found two lovers stark naked on the rocks. The first cab was a 1930 vintage L-4. This was replaced in 1948 by the present L-4 cab, and staffed through the mid-1970's. It was refurbished and placed on the Recreation Rental program in 1986 ... Known lookout personnel: 1967: John & Debra Hubenthal.

evidence.supports: original lookout constructed early 1920s, replaced 1948, named for Anderson/Baker conversation
evidence.quote: The original lookout was constructed in the early 1920s and replaced by the current lookout in 1948.

evidence.supports: cabin dimensions, sleeps 4, amenities, elevation 5772 ft
evidence.quote: The 14x14-ft. lookout has windows on all sides and is encircled by a catwalk. The cabin sleeps 4 people and is equipped 2 twin size beds with mattresses.

evidence.supports: views of Clark Fork Valley, Bitterroot and Cabinet ranges
evidence.quote: It offers panoramic views of Clarks Fork Valley, the Bitterroot Mountains to the west and the Cabinet Range to the east.

evidence.supports: driving directions from Cabinet Ranger Station, seasonal closure on easterly loop segment
evidence.quote: From Cabinet Ranger Station, travel approximately 11 miles southeast on Highway 200 and turn right onto Big Beaver Creek Road 152 (Faro Lane).

corrections.why: The two sources disagree on when the first (pre-1948) lookout cab was built; the brief's '1920' is one of two plausible readings, not a confirmed date.

notes_for_editor: Flagging a date conflict on the pre-1948 lookout (early 1920s vs. 1930-vintage) rather than picking one; worth a look if a primary FS record turns up.
